stories.title: Strategist: Higher bond yields are here to stay
stories.summary: A market strategist argues there are structural reasons elevated bond yields will persist rather than reverse, according to MarketWatch. The piece frames higher yields as a durable backdrop for markets rather than a temporary spike. Specific yield levels, timeframes, and the underlying rationale weren't detailed in the available reporting.

stories.title: Yen rally cools a week after US-Japan currency intervention
stories.summary: The yen's rally following last week's joint U.S.-Japan currency intervention has begun to fade, with traders now shifting focus to upcoming policy signals, according to CNBC. The fading momentum suggests markets are questioning whether intervention alone can sustain yen strength without follow-through policy action.
stories.whyItMatters: Swings in the yen ripple through carry trades, Japanese equities, and global currency markets that macro investors track closely.
whatToWatch: Bank of Japan policy signals
Any further intervention from Japanese authorities
U.S. Treasury or Fed commentary affecting dollar-yen
questions: What specific policy moves are markets waiting on to sustain the yen?
Would authorities intervene again if the rally fully unwinds?

stories.title: Hungary's inflation slows to 1.2% in July

stories.whyItMatters: Cooling inflation gives Hungary's central bank more room to consider rate cuts, a dynamic global macro investors watch across emerging European markets.

stories.title: Wildfire costs surge as much of Europe's damage goes uninsured
stories.summary: Wildfire-related costs are climbing, but a large share of the resulting property damage in Europe isn't covered by insurance, according to CNBC. The coverage gap leaves governments and property owners exposed to a growing share of climate-related losses.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising, under-insured climate losses can pressure reinsurance costs and government budgets, a growing factor in how markets price climate risk.
whatToWatch: Insurer and reinsurer commentary on wildfire exposure
Any policy response from European governments on coverage gaps
questions: How large is the total uninsured damage?

stories.title: Asked to sign as executor without seeing the will — should you refuse?
stories.summary: A MarketWatch reader advice column addresses a case where someone was asked to sign as executor for their brother's estate documents without being allowed to read them first. The piece examines the risks of agreeing to serve as executor without reviewing the underlying paperwork.
stories.whyItMatters: Executor duties carry real financial and legal responsibility, making this relevant to readers managing family estate and financial planning.
whatToWatch: Legal guidance on an executor's right to review documents before signing
questions: What protections exist for someone asked to serve as an executor sight-unseen?

stories.title: SK Hynix to invest $38 billion in new memory chip plants amid soaring demand
stories.summary: SK Hynix plans to invest $38 billion to build new memory chip plants as demand for memory chips surges, according to CNBC. The commitment signals confidence that current demand, driven substantially by AI infrastructure buildout, will continue.
stories.whyItMatters: A large capex commitment from a top memory maker is a direct signal of how strong AI-driven chip demand is expected to remain, with implications for supply, pricing, and rivals like Micron and Samsung.
whatToWatch: Timeline and location details for the new plants
Capacity ramp and its effect on memory chip pricing
Competitor capex responses from Samsung and Micron
questions: Over what timeframe will the $38 billion be deployed?
